title: Contract 1.25.0: runners declare specs, a generic result event, a runner template registry

story.i_want_to: runners to declare which spec templates they hold and report a non-triage spec's result through one event
story.so_that: a new spec ships as a spec, a template and an eval set, without a new socket event

rationale: Today each kind has its own result event (triage_verdict) and the runner's work/3 has one clause per kind (control.ex:1812-1883).

acceptance_criteria.description: RunnerJoin gains optional specs: [{id, version}]; loopctl derives eligibility from it in kind_supported/4 and stores nothing per runner. A runner that sends no specs is read as declaring each of its kinds at version 1, so today's runners are unaffected.
A generic agent_result event carries a spec id, version and a result object validated against that spec's JSON schema; triage keeps triage_verdict. Byte limits and the enum-only audit rule apply.

loopctl-runner holds a template registry keyed {id, version}; work/3 dispatches through it; implement@1 and triage@1 are its first two entries, built from today's prompts unchanged; the branch-prefix exemption comes from the archetype.
The contract version is 1.25.0 in both repos, and the contract test in each binds the vendored copy.

test_cases.name: old runner unaffected
expected_results: eligible for its declared kinds exactly as before

test_cases.name: spec eligibility
expected_results: selected for reply_draft, not for implement

test_cases.name: result validated
steps: send agent_result failing the spec schema

test_cases.name: templates unchanged
steps: render implement@1 and triage@1 from the registry

technical_notes: Repos: loopctl and loopctl-runner. loopctl ships first; the runner upgrade follows.
Each new kind still needs a dispatch_records kind CHECK migration and a Kinds.all entry: the registry test in US-48.2 fails until they agree.
